answerNotes.SHIRT: A shirt has separate parts such as a collar, sleeves, and cuffs. Naming the part helps distinguish it from the whole garment.
answerNotes.SHEET: Sheet can name paper, bed linen, or a flat baking pan. The scene tells whether the material is paper, cloth, or metal.
answerNotes.SUN: The Sun is a star. Its closeness makes it look much larger and brighter than the points of light seen at night.
answerNotes.HANG: Hang means support something from above. A hook, cord, or branch can hold the weight while the object hangs below.
answerNotes.DRY: Dry can be an adjective or an action. It can describe laundry after airing or what happens when moisture leaves a flower bundle.
answerNotes.BASKET: A basket is made by weaving flexible material. Its open structure and carrying handle make it useful for collecting garden produce.
answerNotes.SOCK: A sock covers the foot inside a shoe. Its heel, toe, and cuff name different parts of the same garment.
answerNotes.TOWEL: Towels absorb water after washing or swimming. Their looped fabric holds more moisture than a smooth hard surface.
answerNotes.POLE: A barber pole's stripes traditionally identify the shop. The moving pattern can make the stripes appear to travel upward or downward.
